title: Hacker Runs Hermes AI Agent Unattended for Post-Exploitation at Thai Finance Ministry

reading.body:
An autonomous AI agent named Hermes was deployed by attackers to conduct reconnaissance against Thailand's Ministry of Finance between June and July 2026. The agent ran unattended, enumerating the ministry's network systems without human intervention in each action. This represents a model or agentic system used outside the conditions it was built for, repurposed from its intended function to automate intrusion tasks.

The attackers combined the AI agent with a custom malware implant called Hades and exploit code targeting known vulnerabilities in infrastructure systems. Evidence of the attack, including stolen credentials, agent logs, and attack tools, was recovered from exposed directories on a Hong Kong server. The deployment would have been prevented by network monitoring that flagged unusual enumeration activity, credential theft detection, or access controls that prevented an unauthenticated agent from querying internal systems.

It is not established whether the Hermes agent was purpose-built for this attack, compromised from legitimate use, or repurposed from a commercial or open-source tool.

summary:
# Summary

Thailand's Ministry of Finance was targeted by attackers using an autonomous AI agent named Hermes between June and July 2026. Security researchers discovered three exposed directories on a Hong Kong server containing attack tools, stolen credentials, and logs showing the Hermes agent operating in unattended mode to enumerate the ministry's network systems. The attackers also deployed a custom malware implant called Hades across Windows and Linux platforms, along with exploit code targeting known vulnerabilities in Apache Hadoop, GlassFish servers, and other infrastructure.

The operator, who appears to be Chinese-speaking based on recovered configuration files, built specialized tools to target the ministry's Hadoop cluster, mail systems, and administrative panels. Researchers identified hardcoded stolen credentials and evidence of web shell deployments on ministry servers. Thailand's national cybersecurity agencies were notified on July 15, 2026, and the attack represents a notable shift toward using AI agents to automate routine reconnaissance and exploitation tasks in government espionage operations.
